_: Nodes this system answers on that are NOT SAP objects.
A *.sicf.xml is a claim: this node exists on a system and travels there.
The ADT facade, the launchpad shell, the dumps and the SQL log are none
of those things -- they are JavaScript, on purpose, and writing a SICF
object for them would say they can be transported, which is false. So
the type of a node is not a field we invent inside somebody else's
format: it is WHERE THE NODE IS DECLARED. A SAP object is ABAP and
travels; an entry here is served by this host and does not.
What this buys, which is Alice's point and the whole track: one
inspectable answer to 'what does this system expose and what implements
it', without pretending everything must become ABAP to be listed.
type   HOST   a function of the JavaScript host. Server and binary; not
the browser preview.
ABAP   a class behind the shim. An entry here rather than a
*.sicf.xml means the class is ours and the NODE is not an
object yet -- true of the OData front, and a real gap
rather than a wording.
PROXY  a destination -- another system answers. Derived from
.local/destinations.json, never written here: a list of
credentials cannot be tracked.
handler  the name the host registers under, so a host can mount from
this registry instead of carrying its own list.
needs    fs   could become CONTENT in the object store later.
state  process state: it needs a LIVE host and never works in
the preview -- a different promise, not a smaller one.

/.text: probes the tree for webapp/flp.html before redirecting to the launchpad

/app.text: express.static over webapp/: the launchpad shell and the apps' files

/app/packs.json.text: tilesOf() reads every pack's manifest from disk for the launchpad

/sap/opu/odata/sap.why: the front is attached beside the runtime it proxies to: the same lines start the child, install the dev loop and refresh ZOSD_STATUS_SRV before a read of it. Pulling the mount out of that would separate it from the thing it mounts.
/sap/opu/odata/sap.text: the OData front: ZCL_STG_HTTP_HANDLER behind the shim, or a proxy to the child that runs it. On a system this node is /IWFND/CL_SODATA_HTTP_HANDLER and an ICF object; ours is not one yet

/sap/bc/adt.text: the ADT facade: 59 registrations of its own, meant to stay JavaScript -- A4H has ADT, this imitates it

/osd/not-served.text: what the facade could not answer, held in this process's memory

/osd/serving.text: which generation this process is serving: how a supervisor knows it is alive

/osd/dumps.text: the runtime errors this process has collected, the way ST22 keeps them

/osd/sql.text: the statement log and the bounded SELECT door this process holds

/osd/classrun.text: the door a served (child) runtime answers F9 through: this process holds the live connection, so a classrun of an already-transpiled class runs here, the same dialog step and rollback-on-dump every other request gets
